workPackages.title: Vault dead-end fixes: dust fast path + DEGRADED recovery
workPackages.goal: Close the two remaining PegCycleVault dead ends: a trivial-excess return locking authorizePayout forever, and a short/ambiguous return with no valid state transition.
steps: Relax authorizePayout to accept balance >= rootSum, transferring exactly rootSum and leaving any excess in the escrow (no new state; this closes the pure stray-donation griefing case)

Add recordDegradedReturn(cycleId, receiptDigest, acceptDegraded) — authorizer-only, callable from OUTBOUND when balance is nonzero but satisfies neither the dust-fast-path nor the exact/minimum condition

Require acceptDegraded == true be set only via a distinct authorization schema field that the authorizer signs after an explicit, separately-logged confirmation step (document the off-chain confirmation protocol in a code comment and in docs/modules/peg-cycle-vault.md)
Add a new terminal DEGRADED state; quarantine the balance identically to FAILED (CREATE2-isolated, cannot contaminate a successor cycle)
Allow authorizeFundingAfterFailure-equivalent successor-cycle creation from DEGRADED

Add tests: a return below minimumReturnUsdg without acceptDegraded=true still reverts (no silent laxity); with the flag, DEGRADED is reached and a fresh cycle can start; balance in DEGRADED is never auto-swept; a trivial 1-unit-excess return via the dust fast path pays exactly rootSum and leaves the excess in place

Add a regression test for the FUNDED-with-expired-payout-authorization case: an authorization signed and then expired before authorizePayout consumes it must renew via the same cancelExpiredFundingAuthorization-family path, not lock principal (design.md section 2.5)
acceptance: A return >= rootSum by any amount pays out exactly rootSum, no more, no less
A nonzero return that is neither >= rootSum nor exactly 0 has a valid transition (DEGRADED) instead of being permanently stuck
recordDegradedReturn reverts unless acceptDegraded is explicitly true in the signed authorization
DEGRADED balance is never automatically moved anywhere by any contract function
An expired payout authorization on a FUNDED cycle renews cleanly instead of locking principal
workPackages.notes: This is the single highest-value correctness fix in the whole design — closes a previously-flagged critical dead end. Do not add any path that auto-sweeps a DEGRADED balance. R4/money-safety-critical: per AGENTS.md, this package needs a fresh-context independent reviewer (someone who has not written this diff) before merge — do not self-approve.

workPackages.title: Payout hardening: sentinel fix, TREE_WIDTH literal, chunked payouts
workPackages.goal: Fix two low-risk contract bugs and add chunked-payout support so a single cycle's proceeds can be distributed to more than 1024 holders.
steps: Fix PayoutCommitment: replace the payoutId != bytes32(0) overload used by PayoutAlreadyFunded with an explicit `funded` boolean per record
Add a regression test proving a repeated authorization for payoutId == bytes32(0) reverts PayoutAlreadyFunded on the second call
Fix HolderSettlement: replace the hardcoded 1024 literal with CanonicalMerkleSum.TREE_WIDTH

Add parent/child chunk structure: commitPayoutChunk(payoutId, chunkIndex, rootHash, rootSum) under the existing single payoutId; enforce sum(chunk.rootSum) == payoutLiability[payoutId] exactly before any chunk is claimable
Add an explicit manifest-closed flag so a partial/abandoned chunk commitment can never leave holders permanently unpayable
Add chunkIndex parameter to HolderSettlement.payEntitlement; key paidEntitlements on (payoutId, chunkIndex, index)
Ship chunking inactive by default (chunk count fixed at 1) with a config path to activate multi-chunk mode later
Add tests: partial chunk set is rejected as claimable, exact-sum-across-chunks is enforced, single-chunk mode behaves identically to today's unchunked path, per-chunk pull payment works

Add a named MAX_CHUNKS_PER_PAYOUT constant (a declared maximum, not an unbounded loop) and a gas-metered test committing+claiming one full, maximally-deep 1024-leaf chunk, plus a second gas-metered test committing and closing out a full MAX_CHUNKS_PER_PAYOUT-chunk cycle, recording the total gas cost of each in the test output per security-and-evidence.md's 'hard maximums for callbacks, launch, claims, user exits, and keeper actions' requirement
acceptance: A repeated bytes32(0) payoutId authorization reverts PayoutAlreadyFunded instead of silently overwriting
HolderSettlement no longer contains a bare 1024 literal
Chunk set is atomic: all-or-nothing claimable, sum invariant holds exactly
Single-chunk mode (today's default) behaves identically to the pre-change contract for existing fixture tests
A full 1024-leaf chunk's commit+claim gas cost is measured and recorded, not just asserted to succeed
A full MAX_CHUNKS_PER_PAYOUT-chunk cycle's total close-out gas cost is measured and recorded

workPackages.title: Durable production cycle store: close the ~16-cycle in-memory recovery ceiling
workPackages.goal: Replace the all-in-memory FixtureCycleStore (RECOVERY_LIMITS.storeCycles=16, no disk persistence, no archiving) with a disk-backed store suitable for a scheduler that creates a new cycle every 20 minutes indefinitely, so the live cycle-count ceiling applies only to active cycles and a process restart recovers from disk rather than losing everything.
steps: Read packages/runner/src/cycle/journal.mjs's RECOVERY_LIMITS and cycle-store.mjs's FixtureCycleStore to confirm the exact current ceiling (storeCycles=16, journalEvents=512 per cycle) before changing anything

Add a new durable-store.mjs: an append-only, disk-backed store keyed by cycleId that persists every committed journal entry to a file (or file-per-cycle directory), reloadable on process restart without depending on in-memory state surviving

Add an archiving policy: once a cycle reaches a terminal state (closed/FAILED/DEGRADED and settled), move it out of the 'active' working set the storeCycles-style ceiling applies to, into an append-only archive directory that is never re-loaded into the hot path — so the ceiling bounds concurrent/recent active cycles, not lifetime history

Keep FixtureCycleStore itself unchanged and in use for existing fixture/unit tests (it is fine as a bounded test double); wire production callers (WP-07's AutomatedCycleService, WP-14's scheduler) to the new durable-store.mjs instead
Add a test proving cycle #17 through #40 (beyond the old 16-cycle ceiling) all create, run, and recover correctly against the durable store
Add a crash-and-restart test: kill the process mid-cycle after 20+ prior cycles have completed, restart, and confirm the active cycle resumes correctly from disk
acceptance: Creating and completing more than 16 cycles in sequence never throws a cycle-count-limit error against the durable store
A process restart after 20+ completed cycles recovers the active cycle correctly by reading from disk, not from in-memory state
Terminal (closed/FAILED/DEGRADED) cycles are archived out of the hot working set and are not re-loaded on every recovery pass
FixtureCycleStore's existing bounded behavior is unchanged for tests that still use it directly
workPackages.notes: Closes a real gap the first draft of this plan left unaddressed: an always-on scheduler running every 20 minutes would otherwise hit a hard store-cycle-count-exceeded error within about 5.3 hours of continuous operation. WP-07 and WP-14 both depend on this landing first. options.text: Active before launch — future-proofs against holder growth immediately, but is the highest-risk new contract surface in the design.
Built and tested now, shipped inactive (chunk count fixed at 1), activated only once real holder count approaches 1024.

ownerDecisions.question: Where should floor-rounding dust go if a token migration or wind-down ever happens?

options.text: Carries forward forever into the next cycle's distributable pool (current running default).
Owner names an explicit destination at wind-down time.

ownerDecisions.question: Distribution-signer custody: a single owner-held key, or an owner-held distribution-signer plus an independent verifier (2-of-2)?

options.text: Single owner-held distribution-signer key, no independent verifier.
Owner-held distribution-signer plus a second, independently-held verifier key; both signatures required before a PayoutAuthorization is producible.

ownerDecisions.question: Add a new on-chain guardian/pause role to ProcessBudget, or rely on the two-layer kill switch (off-chain pause flag + on-chain key revocation) only?

options.text: Add an on-chain guardian pause role on ProcessBudget.
No new on-chain role; rely on the off-chain pause flag plus on-chain vault-authorizer/policy-wallet key revocation via the existing two-step MoneyRoles.sol handover.

ownerDecisions.question: Confirm the fee-split reading: does the transcript's '0.5% treasury' mean the currently-coded 0.40% treasury + 0.10% Programmable combined share, or a literal 0.5% treasury bucket carved out separately from Programmable's 0.10% (which would change the 2.50% process-budget figure and require a FeeAccounting.sol behavior change, not just a REQ-text update)?

options.text: Confirm the currently-coded 0.10% Programmable + 0.40% treasury reading (they sum to the transcript's 0.5%) — no contract change beyond WP-02's cumulative-remainder mechanics, WP-02/WP-21 proceed as scoped.
The transcript meant something else — state the owner's actual intended split; treat it as a FeeAccounting.sol bucket-percentage change scoped alongside WP-02.

ownerDecisions.recommended: n/a — this is a factual question about what the owner meant, not an engineering trade-off; no default is assumed

ownerDecisions.question: HookemonIssuance.sol already fixes total supply (420,690,000,000 scaled units) and the 90%/10% market/remainder split in code, with zero owner pre-mint. What should remainderRepresentation (the 10% custody destination) actually be, and what LBP price-curve parameters (starting price, duration/decay) should CustomLaunchStrategy use to execute the 90% market allocation?

options.text: Owner names both the remainder-custody contract and the LBP curve parameters now, so WP-20 is fully scoped before it starts.

WP-20 proceeds against a documented placeholder (a simple timelocked treasury multisig for remainderRepresentation, a conservative default LBP curve) that the owner can override before the actual mainnet launch call, never before — safe because nothing executes against real funds until explicitly promoted per the 'blocked on funded wallets' gate.

ownerDecisions.question: How much operational-response investment is the protocol-fee-brick risk (design.md section 3.7 — Uniswap governance setting a nonzero protocol fee bricks every swap on the pool with no on-chain remedy) worth, beyond the monitoring/alert WP-16 already builds?

options.text: Monitoring/alert only (WP-16, already scoped and unblocked by this decision) — the owner is paged the moment it happens and decides the response live.
Monitoring plus a documented pool-migration runbook prepared in advance (new hook deployment + a defined re-launch path), so the response is not designed from scratch during an incident.
Both, plus a standing pre-authorized automated response (e.g., auto-pause the scheduler on detection) that does not wait for a human.
